per_line.source_text: +**Locked invite-duration AND redemption rule (2026-10-18 clarification `ACCESS-SINGLE-USE-CODES-20261018-01`):** Every **new portal-generated code admits exactly ONE verified email account, once only**, with **no automatic calendar expiry before redemption**. After one successful new-account redemption it is *used*, never reusable for another account, even if that account is later disabled. The unused code remains valid until first redemption or explicit administrator revocation. The generation interface must **NOT** offer 5-use or unlimited-use codes, and the **server** must also enforce `max_uses=1` (not trust an edited browser field). This narrowly supersedes only the provisional multi-use invitation choices in the prior October 18 §4.5 wording; it does not alter the permanent member/admin role decision. The existing database has nullable `expires_at`/`max_uses` for **historic** codes; never silently modify preexisting issued/redeemed rows or weaken past explicit revocations. Revoking an invite must **never revoke a successfully admitted account**. Secure plaintext code generated server-side via 2 independent PostgreSQL cryptographic v4 UUIDs (~244-bit unpredictability), prefixed `dic-`, SHA-256 hash stored privately, shown only once to administrator; never list or store raw codes in GitHub, browser storage or logs. Administrator-only management functions must enforce admission/admin on the **server**, deny anon/nonadmin, maintain non-secret audit receipts and bound active issuance.
per_line.behavior: One verified email redemption/code, no expiry before use, hashed single-display code, server max_uses=1, preserve historic invites.

per_line.source_text: +**Latest owner scope clarification (2026-10-18, ACCESS-REVERSIBLE-REMOVE-ONLY-20261018-01, Locked):** Owner explicitly decided: “I don’t think we need an actual account deletion, remove Access would be sufficient, don’t you?” The product's **entire beta member-removal workflow is administrator-only Remove Access / Restore Access**. This is a reversible admission change (`private.beta_members.enabled=false/true`), **not deletion** of a Supabase Auth user, membership/identity row, private setup, shot, shot rating, personal note, recipe or durable anonymized Community contribution. When removed, members cannot use member-gated application endpoints; existing Supabase sign-in tokens may persist until ordinary expiry, so every protected read/write must check current server admission and RLS. Restoring admission makes the same user's saved data available again. The server must deny attempts to remove *any* administrator, including the owner. **Do not build, expose, or use a member-account hard-delete endpoint or cascading Auth deletion as an admin portal feature**. The current database's foreign keys include `ON DELETE CASCADE` to `auth.users` for personal shots and related tables, so out-of-band hard deletion is **not proven safe** for shot retention and must not be presented as such. If independent user-initiated legal erasure is needed in the future, design a separate consent/privacy-preserving retention and anonymization workflow, with explicit new owner review, security/legal requirements, and actual tests; it is **not part of this initial beta**. This clarification narrows the earlier potential deletion requirement; it does not override any earlier Locked retention, privacy, role, beta, invitation, or no-automatic-expiration requirements.
per_line.behavior: No hard-delete server feature; reversible beta admission/RLS, no cascade deletion of Auth history/notes/Community.
